paper_metadata.title: Quantum Encoding and Analysis on Continuous Time Stochastic Process with Financial Applications

experiments.description: State preparation and quantum-enhanced valuation of a European call option under the Merton Jump Diffusion model using a Lévy-process QCTSP encoding and amplitude-estimation-based extraction.

algorithm.variant: QCTSP preparation plus quantum-enhanced Monte Carlo / amplitude estimation for option pricing

problem_formulation.objective_function: price = max{S0 * exp(D + B_T + sum_{j=1}^{Poi(T)} J_j) - K, 0}, with D = (r - sigma^2/2 - lambda(m + v^2/2))T

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing in the Merton Jump Diffusion model with discontinuous jumps and Brownian motion.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic parameter sweep over jump mean m and jump volatility v; compared against Merton formula, Black-Scholes price, and classical Monte Carlo.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare holding times via exponential subcircuits Exp(lambda T), jump sizes via normal subcircuits Norm(m, v), drift/Brownian term via Norm((r - sigma^2/2 - lambda(m + v^2/2))T, sigma*sqrt(T)); use subtractors, controlled-subtractors, adders, X gates, CNOTs, and a target-qubit rotation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure or apply amplitude estimation to estimate option price; compare against 40-term truncated Merton formula and classical Monte Carlo.

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum-enhanced Monte Carlo / amplitude estimation applied to continuous-time stochastic processes
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims quadratic speedup in the information extraction stage; the option-pricing simulation itself is compared numerically against classical Monte Carlo and a truncated Merton formula, but no explicit runtime benchmark is reported.

experiments.description: Simulation and estimation of ultimate ruin probability in the Collective Risk Model using QCTSP preparation and history-sensitive extraction with flag qubits.

algorithm.variant: QCTSP-based ruin probability estimation with controlled subtraction and flag-qubit history tracking

problem_formulation.objective_function: psi(u) = P[X(tau) < 0 | X(0)=u, tau < infinity], with X(t) = u + ct - sum_{j=1}^{Poi(t)} xi_j
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Flag qubits record whether the running surplus crosses below zero; controlled subtraction and CNOT-based flag updates detect first ruin event.

problem_instance.description: Ultimate ruin probability under the Collective Risk (Cramér-Lundberg) model.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic insurance risk process with Poisson claim arrivals and exponential inter-claim times; evaluated for varying initial surplus and sample path lengths.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare claim arrival process and claim sizes; compute running surplus via adders and modified subtractors; use a flag register to detect first hitting/ruin event.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure the flag/indicator to estimate ruin probability; compare against theoretical benchmark.

speedup_claims.conditions: for the QCTSP-based quantum-enhanced Monte Carlo framework used to estimate ruin probability and other path-dependent quantities
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states a quadratic speedup for the Monte Carlo component, but does not provide a direct runtime comparison for ruin probability estimation.
